reasons.text: Certificates claim more than the declared monthly capacity in 89% of months
80% of feedstock comes from collectors invoicing far beyond their declared capacity
Electricity bought is only 0.35x the minimum needed for the tonnes claimed (104 kWh/t against at least 300)
66% of purchase invoices have suspiciously round tonnages (typical plant: about 2%)
Sold products equal only 23% of the output expected from the tonnes claimed
55% of high-value consignments have no e-way bill

inspection_checklist: Check installed machinery and shift records against the declared capacity; request production registers for the flagged months.
Visit the named collectors: confirm premises, vehicles and storage; check their registration dates and sales to other buyers.
Obtain the DISCOM consumption statement and meter readings for the flagged months; compare connected machinery (kW) against the claimed tonnage.
Physically verify a sample of purchase invoices with the sellers (weighbridge slips, e-way bills, vehicle logs).
Reconcile product sales with processed tonnes; contact the product buyers listed and verify that they received the material.
